# Nissaraṇiya Sutta (Iti 72 (It 3.23 PTS It 61))

**ID:** Iti 72 (It 3.23 PTS It 61)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Nissaraṇiya Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nissaraṇiya Sutta* ("Elements of Escape") is the 72nd discourse of the *Itivuttaka*, located in the third section (It 3.23, PTS p. 61) [Windisch 1889]. Delivered with the traditional *Itivuttaka* framing, the discourse expounds three properties or elements of escape (*tisso nissaraṇiyā dhātuyo*): renunciation (*nekkhamma*) as the escape from sensuality (*kāma*); the formless (*āruppa*) as the escape from forms (*rūpa*); and cessation (*nirodha*) as the escape from whatever is produced, conditioned, and dependently arisen (*bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ*) [Windisch 1889]. The teaching concludes with verses declaring that a monk who thoroughly comprehends the escape from forms and the stilling of all conditioned things (*sabbasaṅkhārasamatha*) attains liberation and arrives at peace through higher knowledge (*abhiññāvosito*) [Windisch 1889].
